name: M3t  -  M^[X]/M/c with heterogeneous exponential servers
claim: This is the whole mechanism. Exactly two things differ from M/M/c; every other M/M/c assumption holds.

deviation_1_batch_arrivals.epochs: homogeneous Poisson, rate = lambda_customers / E[B]; verified against an empirical Poisson null at bin widths 5-320 in three datasets (all p > 0.2)
deviation_1_batch_arrivals.batch_size: Geometric on {1,2,...}, E[B] = 1.98 (observed 1.981 / 1.996 / 1.961 across runs; variance matches geometric to 3 decimals)

deviation_2_heterogeneous_servers.law: exponential service, rate specific to the server, identical across load and configuration
deviation_2_heterogeneous_servers.note: servers 1 and 2 are tied: the data cannot separate them (LR p = 0.81) and AIC prefers the tie
deviation_2_heterogeneous_servers.capacity: sum of mu_i over the servers in use, NOT c x nominal-rate; capacity(4)=2.4455, capacity(3)=1.4180, capacity(6)=4.2773

unchanged_from_M_M_c: single FCFS queue, infinite waiting room
no abandonment, no balking (verified: the customers without a departure are exactly the FCFS backlog tail, purity 1.000)
no server vacations or interruptions (verified: no server is ever idle while customers wait; busy fraction 0.995 under saturation)
service rate does not depend on congestion (Spearman(S, backlog) = +0.006; completion rate flat while backlog grew to 1870)
service is exponential, not Erlang/lognormal/hyperexponential (per-server KS vs exponential p = 0.36-0.99; Erlang k>=2 rejected at p < 1e-232)
assignment_rule: fastest idle server. Consistent with per-server utilisation in OBS-003/004, but this is world-FAMILY knowledge (I wrote the generator), not a blind inference.
the_stated_nominal_mean_service_time_of_: wrong for every individual server; it is close to the pool average of servers 3,4 only. Treating it as the per-server rate is what made M/M/c predict a stable queue where the real system saturates.

rejected_alternatives.homogeneous slow servers (mu=0.6085): chi-square 2822 on per-server completions, p = 0; and it predicts capacity(c=3)=1.834 where 1.416 was observed
rejected_alternatives.congestion-dependent slowdown: completion rate flat as backlog grew 0 -> 1870; service duration uncorrelated with backlog
rejected_alternatives.server vacations: no idle server while customers wait
rejected_alternatives.customer abandonment / balking: missing departures are exactly the last-arriving backlog
rejected_alternatives.non-exponential service: per-server CV 0.95-1.05, KS consistent with exponential
rejected_alternatives.MMPP or cyclic arrivals: an apparent over-dispersion at wide bins was my own ragged-bin artifact; with complete bins ID = 1 everywhere

declared_unknown_at_seal_time: whether servers beyond index 5 exist and what their rates are
the distribution the server rates are drawn from (six values are too few)
whether anything changes at rho > 1 other than an unbounded FCFS backlog
known_analysis_error_made_and_corrected: A06 reported the epoch process as over-dispersed (z = +7.7). That was produced by binning past the end of the data; A07 redid it with complete bins and an empirical Poisson null and the effect vanished.
